question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Robert Clive's early life and arrival in India]
options: Clive's birthplace — Styche Hall, Market Drayton, Shropshire, England
Clive's employer on arrival in India — East India Company as a writer (clerk)
Port of Clive's first arrival in India — Madras (Fort St. George)
Clive's first posting in India — Bombay (Fort William)
wrong_fact: Clive's first posting was at Madras (Fort St. George), not Bombay. Fort William is the name of the British fort in Calcutta, not Bombay.
explanation: Robert Clive was born at Styche Hall, Market Drayton, Shropshire in 1725. He arrived in India in 1744 as a writer (clerk) for the East India Company and was first posted at Fort St. George, Madras. Fort William is located in Calcutta (Kolkata), not Bombay (Mumbai). His early years in Madras were reportedly difficult, and he is said to have attempted suicide twice.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [British forts and their locations in 18th-century India]
options: Fort St. David — Cuddalore, Coromandel Coast
wrong_fact: Fort St. Angelo is located at Kannur (Cannanore) on the Malabar Coast of Kerala, not in Bombay. The main British fort in Bombay was Bombay Castle.
explanation: Fort St. George (Madras), Fort St. David (Cuddalore), and Fort William (Calcutta) were all key East India Company fortifications. Fort St. Angelo was originally built by the Portuguese at Kannur in Kerala and later came under British control. The British fortification in Bombay was Bombay Castle. Clive served at Fort St. David during the First Carnatic War, which was a formative period in his early career.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Events and locations during Clive's early career in India 1744–1751]
options: French siege of Madras (1746) — Fort St. George, Madras
Clive's escape to British territory after French capture of Madras — Fort St. David, Cuddalore
Battle of Adyar (1746) — Adyar River, near Madras
Clive's first military commission — Bombay Marine, Bombay
wrong_fact: Clive received his first military commission in the East India Company's army at Madras, not in the Bombay Marine. He was commissioned as an Ensign in the Madras infantry in 1747.
explanation: When the French under La Bourdonnais captured Madras in 1746, Clive escaped to Fort St. David at Cuddalore. The Battle of Adyar (Battle of St. Thomé) took place near the Adyar River south of Madras. Clive's military career began when he received a commission as an Ensign in the East India Company's Madras army in 1747 — not in the Bombay Marine, which was a separate naval force based in Bombay.
